parameter_name: Ryegrass juice nitrogen precipitated by isoelectric treatment
normalized_si_unit: kg N/kg N in cleared juice
basis: precipitated N / total N in cleared juice
extraction_method: screw-pressed and mildly centrifuged; 6 M HCl to pH 4–4.5
operating_conditions: 2000 g grass sample; 1 mm screen; pulp re-pressed with 1:1 demineralized water; clearing 500 g, 1 min; 30 mL aliquots; precipitate separated at 4000 g for 20 min
source_title: Enhancing Protein Recovery in Green Biorefineries by Lignosulfonate-Assisted Precipitation
source_location: Conclusion; Figure 5; Materials and Methods (precipitation pH)
notes: Conclusion reports 38% relative N precipitation for ryegrass under isoelectric conditions. This is total-N precipitation, not isolated protein recovery; the study used a double-press procedure with added wash water and prior juice clarification. Figure 5 reports mean ± SD (n=3); the exact SD is plotted but not tabulated in article text.
uncertainty: n=3; SD plotted; no numeric SD in article text
transferability_to_grass: Published ryegrass evidence; proxy for roadside grass and the GreenHub single-press juice boundary

parameter_name: Scalar pH candidate selected from the reported ryegrass isoelectric-precipitation interval
basis: Reported interval pH 4.0–4.5; upper endpoint selected as scalar candidate
protein_source: crude protein and other precipitable nitrogen
operating_conditions: Screw-pressed ryegrass; pulp re-pressed with 1:1 demineralized water; juices mixed and cleared; acidified to pH 4–4.5
valid_range: Source range 4.0–4.5; 4.5 is the selected endpoint, not a unique optimum
source_title: Enhancing Protein Recovery in Green Biorefineries by Lignosulfonate-Assisted Precipitation
source_location: Materials and Methods, Sample Preparation and Precipitation; Results and Discussion, lines 334–338 and 391–393
notes: The article reports the interval pH 4–4.5 for acid isoelectric precipitation and states that this is typically the optimum interval; the model candidate uses only its upper endpoint as a scalar. It is not a GreenHub-specific measured setpoint.
uncertainty: No statistical uncertainty is reported for the interval; choosing one scalar endpoint is an explicit model assumption.
transferability_to_grass: Direct ryegrass process comparator, but cultivated Danish laboratory juice and double pressing differ from Dutch roadside feed and GreenHub's configured boundary.
